permutationLabel: Failed Gastrografin challenge (contrast not in colon at 24 h), day 3
summary: 71-year-old woman on day 3 of NOM for adhesive SBO; contrast has not reached the colon at 24 h, NG output 1.6 L/day, no flatus, no strangulation signs.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Ongoing vomiting and distension, day 3 of admission
inputs.hpi: Admitted 3 days ago with adhesive small bowel obstruction (previous open right hemicolectomy). Managed with NG tube, IV fluids and nil by mouth. 100 mL Gastrografin given 30 hours ago: the 24-hour film shows contrast still in dilated small bowel, none in the colon. NG output 1.6 L in 24 h. No flatus. Pain colicky, not worse. No fever.

exam.abdomen: Distended, tympanic, mild diffuse tenderness, no guarding or rebound. NG tube draining bilious fluid.

imaging.name: Abdominal X-ray 24 h after water-soluble contrast
imaging.result: Contrast remains within dilated small bowel loops; no contrast has reached the colon at 24 hours.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Adhesive small bowel obstruction — failed non-operative management
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Adhesive small bowel obstruction, day 3 of non-operative management: water-soluble contrast has not reached the colon at 24 h and NG output remains high. Non-operative management has failed — surgery (laparoscopic or open adhesiolysis).

mustInclude.note: Bologna: contrast not in the colon at 24 h predicts failure of NOM; NOM beyond 72 h without progress increases morbidity and mortality — operate.

mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a 'failed NOM' variant (contrast not in colon at 24 h, no resolution by 72 h) with immediate + surgical phases.

mustExclude.note: The challenge has been done and failed; repeating it delays surgery.
An appendicectomy operative plan in an SBO patient can only come from the negated exam text ('no guarding or rebound').

guideline.name: WSES Bologna guidelines — adhesive small bowel obstruction (2017 update)
guideline.section: CT with IV contrast for strangulation signs; non-operative management (NGT, fluids) up to 72 h without strangulation; water-soluble contrast challenge (colon within 24 h predicts success); surgery for strangulation, peritonitis or failed NOM; virgin abdomen and hernia causes
guideline.citation: ten Broek RPG, Krielen P, Di Saverio S, et al. Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO): 2017 update of the evidence-based guidelines from the WSES ASBO working group. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:24.

rationale: Permutation: the water-soluble contrast challenge result. A failed challenge (no contrast in the colon at 24 h) and no progress by day 3 mean surgery (Bologna), so the plan must move from NOM to operation.
